Figure 1:Text-to-image generation without internet-scale language pretraining.Left:Generation quality on GPIC(Chandrasegaran et al., 2026)(gFD, log scale) vs. total pretraining FLOPs required to build each T2I system, including language model, image tokenizer, and image generator pretraining.
Each⋆\starmarks total pretraining FLOPs and gFD, while the donut breaks down language and vision compute.Halcyon (Ours), trained entirely from scratch, achieves lower gFD with substantially lower total pretraining computecompared to:(i) LlamaGen(Sun et al., 2024), late-fusion autoregressive models with 0.78–0.90B image generators and pretrained FLAN-T5 encoders (0.11–1.22B);(ii) JiT-T2I(Li and He, 2026;Ma et al., 2026), late-fusion diffusion models with a 1.10B image generator and pretrained Qwen3-1.7B; and(iii) Qwen3-0.6B-CPT, an autoregressive model continually pretrained on image–text pairs, initialized from a pretrained Qwen3-0.6B language model(Yang et al., 2025a).Right:256×256256\times 256samples generated by Halcyon-4B with prompts shown for two samples.
Best viewed in color.

Figure 5:Comparison of generated images.From left to right: JiT-T2I-XXL/8++, LlamaGen-XL/8, and Halcyon models from 0.1B to 4B parameters.
For the baselines, we report the sizes of thelanguage modelandimage generatorseparately.
Image quality improves asHalcyonscales up.
All prompts are from GPIC Test-50K.
Additional samples are provided in AppendixD.

Figure 6:Image captioning examples fromHalcyon-4B.For each example, the ground-truth caption is shown above the input image, and the generated caption is shown below.
The model learns image captioning by replacing caption-dropped T2I examples with I2T supervision, using only 10% of the pretraining budget for captioning.
